sources.design: Randomised three-arm trial, n=74; 14 withdrew for inadequate progress.
sources.population: Athletes older than 16 with symptoms longer than three weeks and diffuse posteromedial tenderness of at least 5 cm. Suspected stress fracture/compartment syndrome was excluded.
sources.comparator: Graded running alone versus added calf stretching/strengthening versus compression stockings.
sources.outcomes: Mean completion time was 105.2, 117.6 and 102.1 days respectively, with no significant between-group difference or satisfaction benefit.
sources.uncertainty: No rest/no-treatment comparator and substantial noncompletion. Trial-screened MTSS pain values cannot be exported to suspected fracture or every severity.
sources.harms: Fourteen did not complete because of inadequate progress; robust harms ascertainment was not established.
sources.limitations: No rest/no-treatment comparator and substantial noncompletion. Trial-screened MTSS pain values cannot be exported to suspected fracture or every severity. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: Six-phase graded walk/run program; adjunct calf stretching/strengthening had five phases. Exact individual exercise variants were not verified from the addendum.
protocol.dose: Phase-specific walk/run duration; no single transferable running dose.
protocol.frequency: Running three times weekly with a rest day between sessions; adjunct exercise five times weekly.
protocol.supervision: Investigators taught/practised exercises, followed by home performance.
protocol.progression: If walking hurt, started after two pain-free walking days. Progression required running pain below 4/10; pain at least 4 afterwards/next day prevented advancement and reduced running by two minutes.
protocol.stoppingRules: Trial-specific rules above. They do not establish fracture clearance or an app-wide pain threshold.

sources.design: Parallel-group RCT, n=40, with a multimodal active comparator.
sources.population: Recreational runners with diagnosed MTSS; mean age 23.9, 40% women.
sources.comparator: Multimodal care versus the same care plus lower-leg exercise.
sources.coInterventions: Both groups used graded walk/run, ice and five shockwave sessions; existing orthoses continued.
sources.outcomes: No added improvement in pain or MTSS severity at six/twelve weeks. Quality-of-life and foot-posture measures improved with added exercise.
sources.uncertainty: Small multimodal trial with no isolated exercise-component effect. Posture/QoL improvement does not establish pain reduction or prevention of bone stress injury. Exercise frequency was not clear in inspected methods.
sources.harms: No side effects reported; questionnaires collected every three weeks.
sources.limitations: Small multimodal trial with no isolated exercise-component effect. Posture/QoL improvement does not establish pain reduction or prevention of bone stress injury. Exercise frequency was not clear in inspected methods. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: Short-foot exercise raises the arch without toe flexion or forefoot lift, progressing seated to double-leg then single-leg stance. Also side-lying band inversion, seated band plantarflexion, weighted towel toe curls, straight-/bent-knee wall stretches and foam rolling.
protocol.dose: Short foot: 5-second holds up to 3 minutes. Band exercises: 3 × 12–15. Toe curls: 3 × 15–20. Stretch: 5 × 20–30 seconds. Rolling: 4 × 45 seconds, 30-second rests.
protocol.frequency: not clearly reported in the inspected intervention section; 12-week program.
protocol.supervision: Clinic-based supervision by an experienced physical therapy/sports science specialist with physician input.
protocol.progression: After 4 × 15 for one week without increased symptoms, increase band/load; sets increased from 3 to 4, with resistance described from 40% to 85% 1 RM.
protocol.stoppingRules: Progression required no worsening; no universal numeric app threshold established.
